tests: Whether an adjacent pair is out of order, and so whether it is swapped (the comparison rule).
examplePrompt: The algorithm is comparing index 0 (value 5) and index 1 (value 3). What should happen next?

tests: What one completed pass guarantees: the largest remaining unsorted value is in its final place (the invariant).
examplePrompt: This pass is now complete. What can we guarantee about the array?
options: Every element was compared exactly once | The entire array is now sorted | The largest remaining unsorted element is now in its correct position | The smallest element moved to the front
correctOption: The largest remaining unsorted element is now in its correct position

tests: What property proves the array is fully sorted: no adjacent pair is out of order.
examplePrompt: Bubble Sort has finished. What proves the array is fully sorted?
options: Every element was compared at least once | Every element was visited the same number of times | No adjacent pair is out of order anywhere in the array | The total number of swaps equals the array length
correctOption: No adjacent pair is out of order anywhere in the array

tests: Estimating how many comparisons the finished run made, relating the count to the growth rate.
examplePrompt: This run sorted 5 elements. Roughly how many comparisons did it make?

tests: Why a pass with no swaps means the array is sorted and the algorithm can stop.
examplePrompt: The algorithm stopped before completing all passes. Why?
options: Equal elements caused the loop to stop | No swaps were needed - the array was already in order | The algorithm completed the maximum number of passes | The first element reached its correct position
correctOption: No swaps were needed - the array was already in order

tests: Comparing the target with the middle value to choose which half can still contain it.
examplePrompt: The midpoint is index 3 (value 7), and the target is 8. What should happen next?
options: 7 equals 8 - target found | 8 is larger - search the right half | 8 is smaller - search the left half
correctOption: 8 is larger - search the right half

tests: What confirms the target was located: an equality check at the index found.
examplePrompt: Binary Search has finished. What confirms the target was correctly located?
options: Every element in the array was visited | The array became sorted during the search | The element at index 3 was confirmed equal to the target | The target was matched at more than one index
correctOption: The element at index 3 was confirmed equal to the target

tests: Estimating how many comparisons the finished run made, relating the count to the growth rate.
examplePrompt: This search ran on 8 sorted elements. How many comparisons with the target did it make?

tests: What confirms the target is absent: the whole search range was eliminated.
examplePrompt: Binary Search has finished without finding the target. What confirms the search correctly covered the whole space?
options: The array must be unsorted for the target to be missing | The entire valid search space was eliminated without a match | The range still had unchecked values when the search stopped | The target could still be found by starting over
correctOption: The entire valid search space was eliminated without a match

tests: Where a new value attaches once an empty position is reached.
examplePrompt: Reached an empty position. Where does 4 belong?
options: Attach as the left child of node 8 | Attach as the right child of node 8 | Compare it against node 8 again
correctOption: Attach as the left child of node 8

tests: Comparing a value with the current node to go left or right (equal values go right).
examplePrompt: At node 8: is 4 smaller, or greater than or equal to it? (Equal values go right in this tree.)
options: 4 is greater than or equal to 8 - go right | 4 is less than 8 - go left | This position is empty - insert here

tests: Which traversal lists any binary search tree in sorted order (in-order), from the ordering invariant.
examplePrompt: The tree is built. Which traversal lists the values of any binary search tree in sorted order?
options: In-order: left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree | Level-order: the root, then each level from left to right | Pre-order: the node first, then its left and right subtrees | Reading the values back in the order they were inserted
correctOption: In-order: left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree

tests: Estimating how many comparisons the finished run made, relating the count to the growth rate.
examplePrompt: Building this tree inserted 7 values. Roughly how many comparisons did the inserts make in total?

tests: How a node is removed without breaking the ordering: leaf, one child, or in-order successor.
examplePrompt: Deleting 4, which has two children. How is it removed without breaking the tree's ordering?
options: Copy in its in-order successor (the smallest value in its right subtree), then remove that node | Delete it together with its right subtree | Remove it and reattach both subtrees to its parent | Replace it with its parent's value
correctOption: Copy in its in-order successor (the smallest value in its right subtree), then remove that node
